blocks.text: Diligent Practice and Steadfast Holding, Chapter Forty-Six

inline.s: [The Buddha told Maitreya: The unsurpassed Dharma of the Buddhas and Tathagatas — the Dharma of the ten powers and fearlessness, the profound Dharma of non-obstruction and non-attachment, and the bodhisattva Dharma of the paramitas — is not easily met. A Dharma-preacher is also hard to find to expound it. Firm and deep faith is likewise hard to encounter.]

The Buddha told Maitreya Bodhisattva: The unsurpassed Dharma of the Buddhas and Tathagatas — the Dharma of the ten powers and fearlessness, the profound Dharma of non-obstruction and non-attachment, and the bodhisattva Dharma of the paramitas — is very hard to encounter. A Dharma-preacher is also hard to find to expound it. One with firm and deep faith is likewise not easily found.

[I now proclaim in accord with truth this vast and subtle Dharma-gate, praised by all the Buddhas. I entrust it to you, to be a great protection, for the long-night benefit of all beings. Do not let them sink into the five realms and suffer every peril and hardship.]

I now proclaim in accord with truth this vast and subtle Pure Land Dharma-gate, praised by all the Buddhas. I entrust it to you, to be a great protection, for the long-night benefit of all beings. Do not let them sink into the five realms and suffer every peril and hardship.
(Entrusting it to you)

Maitreya Bodhisattva is a bodhisattva of the one lifetime that remains, presently dwelling in the inner court of the Tushita heaven. After four thousand years (that is, five hundred and sixty-seven million years in human time), he will descend to be born in the human world, and beneath the dragon-flower tree in the Grove of Flowers he will attain Buddhahood, succeeding Shakyamuni Buddha as the fifth Buddha of the Fortunate Age.
“The Buddha told Maitreya:
I now proclaim in accord with truth this vast and subtle Dharma-gate, praised by all the Buddhas. I entrust it to you, to be a great protection, for the long-night benefit of all beings.”
This shows that after Maitreya Bodhisattva attains Buddhahood in this Saha world, he too will proclaim and spread the Sutra of Measureless Life.
(The long night) A metaphor for the long darkness of ignorance in which ordinary beings, from beginningless kalpas, drift through birth and death.

[You should diligently practice, following my teaching. Be filial to the Buddha, ever mindful of the teacher's grace. Cause this Dharma to endure long without perishing. Hold fast to it, and do not destroy or lose it. Do not recklessly add to or subtract from the sutra's Dharma.]

You should diligently practice, following my teaching. Be filial to the Buddha, ever mindful of the grace of your original teacher. Cause this Dharma to endure long without perishing. Hold fast to it, and do not destroy or lose it. Do not recklessly add to or subtract from the sutra's Dharma.

[Ever mindful without interruption, one swiftly attains the Way. My Dharma is thus, and I speak it thus. What the Tathagata practices, you should likewise practice. Plant and cultivate merit and virtue, and seek rebirth in the pure land.]

Those who are ever mindful of the name of Amitabha Buddha without interruption swiftly attain the Way. My Dharma is thus, and I speak it thus. What the Tathagata practices, you should likewise practice. Plant and cultivate merit and virtue, and seek rebirth in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss.
(Ever mindful without interruption) 'Ever mindful' means being ever mindful of the name of Amitabha Buddha; 'without interruption' means thought after thought continuing without break.

blocks.text: Heard through Merit and Wisdom, Chapter Forty-Seven

inline.s: [At that time, the World-Honored One spoke a verse:
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke a verse:
If in past lives you did not plant merit and wisdom, this true Dharma you
cannot hear
(you fail to hear the Pure Land Dharma-gate, or though you hear it you cannot believe it and take it in);
but those who have already made offerings to the Tathagatas are then able to rejoice and believe in this matter.
The evil, the proud, the slothful, and the wrong-viewed find it hard to believe the Tathagata's subtle Dharma; like the blind who forever dwell in darkness, they cannot guide others along the path.
Only those who have planted all virtue before the Buddha can cultivate this world-saving practice
(the Pure Land Dharma-gate)
; having heard it, they receive and hold it, copy it, recite it, praise and proclaim it, and make offerings to it.
(The world-saving practice) The Pure Land Dharma-gate can broadly deliver living beings out of birth and death, and so it is called the world-saving practice.

Thus, with single-minded heart seeking the pure land, one is certain to be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss; even should a great fire fill the three-thousand worlds, riding the Buddha's majestic virtue one can pass beyond it all.

The Tathagata's deep and vast sea of wisdom only a Buddha with a Buddha can know; though shravakas ponder the Buddha's wisdom for ten thousand kalpas, exhausting their spiritual powers they cannot measure it.
The Tathagata's merit the Buddha himself knows; only the World-Honored One can reveal it. Human birth is hard to obtain and a Buddha is hard to meet
(hard to encounter)
; to hear the Dharma with faith and wisdom is the hardest of all.
If any being is to become a Buddha, his practice must surpass Samantabhadra's and reach the farther shore; therefore you of wide learning and wisdom should believe my teaching, the word of truth.

Such is this subtle Dharma, fortunate indeed to be heard: you should ever recite the Buddha and give rise to joy; receiving and holding it, you can broadly cross the stream of birth and death — the Buddha says such a person is a true good friend.]

(Receiving, holding, and broadly crossing the stream of birth and death) To receive and hold this sutra and, by this Pure Land Dharma-gate, widely save those beings who are sinking in the stream of birth and death. 'The stream' means persons of the same kind. 'The stream of birth and death' means the stream of birth and death, that is, beings sunk in birth and death. (The Buddha says such a person is a true good friend) The Buddha says such a person is truly a good friend of beings (a good spiritual friend).

blocks.text: Hearing the Sutra and Gaining Benefit, Chapter Forty-Eight

inline.s: [At that time, when the World-Honored One had spoken this sutra and Dharma, in the world of gods and humans twelve thousand kotis of billions of beings, free from dust and defilement, attained the pure Dharma-eye. Twenty billion beings attained the fruit of the non-returner. Six thousand eight hundred bhikshus, their outflows exhausted, realized liberation of mind. Forty billion bodhisattvas abided in non-retrogression from the supreme bodhi, adorning themselves with the merit of the great vows. Two and a half billion beings attained the patience of non-retrogression. Four trillion kotis of hundreds of billions of beings, who had never before roused the thought for the supreme bodhi, now for the first time roused it. Planting all manner of wholesome roots, they vowed to be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, to see Amitabha Buddha, and shall all be reborn in that Tathagata's land. Each in a different direction, they will successively attain Buddhahood, all bearing the same name — the Tathagata Wondrous Sound.]
At that time, when the World-Honored One had finished speaking this sutra and Dharma, in the world of gods and humans twelve thousand kotis of billions of beings, free from dust and defilement
(afflictions)

, attained the pure Dharma-eye. Twenty billion beings attained the fruit of the non-returner. Six thousand eight hundred bhikshus, their afflictions exhausted, realized liberation of mind. Forty billion bodhisattvas abided in non-retrogression from the supreme bodhi, adorning themselves with the merit of the great vows. Two and a half billion beings attained the patience of non-retrogression. Four trillion kotis of hundreds of billions of beings, who had never before roused the thought for the supreme bodhi, now for the first time roused it. Planting all manner of wholesome roots, they vowed to be born in the Land of Ultimate Bliss, to see Amitabha Buddha, and shall all be reborn in the Western Land of Ultimate Bliss. Each in a world of the ten directions, they will successively attain Buddhahood, all bearing the same name — the Tathagata Wondrous Sound.
(Afflictions exhausted) One has attained the fruit of arhatship.

[Again, in the Buddha-lands of the ten directions, whether living now or to be reborn in the future, all who see Amitabha Buddha — each land has eighty thousand kotis of billions of beings who receive the prophecy, attain the patience of the Dharma, and accomplish the supreme bodhi. Those beings, all through the conditions of Amitabha Buddha's past vows, shall together be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.]

Again, among the Buddha-lands of the ten directions, whether those beings are living now or are to be reborn in the future, all who see Amitabha Buddha — each land has eighty thousand kotis of billions of beings who receive the prophecy, attain the patience of the Unborn Dharma, and accomplish the supreme bodhi (perfectly realizing Buddhahood). These beings, all through the conditions of Amitabha Buddha's past vows, shall together be reborn in the Land of Ultimate Bliss.
(Koti) A number used in ancient India, equivalent to today's one hundred million.

[At that time, the three-thousand-great-thousand world shook in six ways, and there appeared all manner of rare spiritual transformations; a great light shone forth, illuminating the ten directions. Again, various devas in the empty sky made wonderful music and gave forth sounds of rejoicing. Even the devas of the realm of form all heard it and exclaimed that never before had there been such a thing. Measureless wondrous flowers rained down in abundance.]

At that time, the three-thousand-great-thousand world shook in six ways, and there appeared all manner of rare spiritual transformations; a great light shone forth, illuminating the ten directions. Again, various devas in the empty sky made wonderful music and gave forth sounds of rejoicing. Even the devas of the realm of form all heard it and exclaimed that never before had there been such a thing. Measureless wondrous flowers rained down in abundance.

[The Venerable Ananda, Maitreya Bodhisattva, and all the bodhisattvas, shravakas, the eight classes of gods and dragons, and the whole assembly, having heard what the Buddha said, were all filled with great joy, and believed, received, and practiced it.]

The Venerable Ananda, Maitreya Bodhisattva, and all the bodhisattvas, shravakas, the eight classes of gods and dragons, and the whole assembly, having heard what the Buddha said, were all filled with great joy, and believed, received, and practiced it.
